doc.title: Yu-Gi-Oh! Genesys Tier List
doc.summary: The Yu-Gi-Oh! Genesys tier list, updated November 6, 2026: Kewl Tune / Synchron holds Tier 1 alone. Ranked from 31,085 YGO Omega ladder games.

infobox.caption: Kewl Tune / Synchron, the leading deck

blocks.md: This Yu-Gi-Oh! Genesys tier list ranks the decks on the YGO Omega Genesys ladder by expected win rate, from ranked games through November 6, 2026. **Kewl Tune / Synchron** holds Tier 1 alone, with an expected 60.3% win rate and 0.7% of the meta.

blocks.title: What this list can't tell you
blocks.md: We rank Genesys decks from ranked YGO Omega games in the Silver+ band, set by each pair's average rating. We adjust for rating gaps and turn order. Specialist pilots, deck choices and anything the game log doesn't record can still move a deck's number, and tournament fields can differ from the ladder.

blocks.caption: Genesys tiers for November 6, 2026: Kewl Tune / Synchron leads at 60.3% expected win rate. Tier 4 shows its top five builds; Others counts the rest.

blocks.md: A deck's tier says how many points of expected win rate it gives up to the leader. For what moved this week, read the [latest meta report](/wiki/yu-gi-oh-meta-report-november-6-2026). For the other ladder, see the [TCG tier list](/wiki/yu-gi-oh-tcg-tier-list), and between updates, the [live statistics page](/statistics?ladder=genesys).

The Genesys ladder is 48 days into the 09.2026 season, with 31,085 games from 1,663 players. The most played deck, Blitzclique, holds 6.8% of the meta. The 15 builds shown below cover 21% of it. We show Tiers 1–3 and the five highest-ranked Tier 4 builds; the [statistics page](/statistics?ladder=genesys) lists the rest. New to the format? blocks.text: Which decks are underplayed and overplayed?

blocks.md:
The underplayed decks reach Tier 2 or better on a small share of the meta. Specialists may pilot most of their games, so test one before you trust its number. The overplayed decks sit among the ten most played and land in Tier 3 or lower.

- **Underplayed:** Angelechy / Dark Time Wizard (0.6% of the meta, expected 59.6%), Kewl Tune / Synchron (0.7% of the meta, expected 60.3%) and Synchron / Elfnote (0.8% of the meta, expected 57.3%)
- **Overplayed:** Blitzclique (6.8% of the meta, expected 57.1%), Hecahands / Chimera (3.5% of the meta, expected 52.1%) and HERO (3.1% of the meta, expected 49.1%)

We show matchups that outperform or underperform the model's expectation for the six highest-ranked builds against Tiers 1–3. We require a 95% interval clear of that expectation and at least 80 games. An above-expected matchup can still have a win rate below 50%.

| Deck | Above expectation | Below expectation |
|---|---|---|
| **Kewl Tune / Synchron** | None clear | None clear |
| **Angelechy / Dark Time Wizard** | None clear | None clear |
| **Angelechy** | None clear | None clear |

| **Archfiend** | None clear | None clear |

Every number comes from ranked games on [YGO Omega](/wiki/ygo-omega-wiki), the same data as the [statistics page](/statistics?ladder=genesys). Below are the settings behind this week's Genesys list. The [statistics methodology](/wiki/ygo-omega-statistics-methodology) explains the model and why we replaced the old ranking score.

We fit the model on Silver+ games. A game's band comes from the average of both players' previous-day ratings, each capped at 3,000, so a Silver+ game can include one player below Silver. Both players need 3 ranked games this season, or we leave the game out. Decklists need no minimum number of games. A deck needs 15 deck-games for its own estimate and a row; smaller decks share one pooled estimate and stay off the list. So far this season, these rules removed 1,108 games for player activity and 66,755 in the Iron band, where the pair averages under Bronze or one side has no rating, out of 119,132 games.

blocks.text: How a deck gets its number

blocks.md: For each decisive game, we fit both deck strengths, the going-first effect and the rating-gap effect. Expected win rate is a deck's predicted result against the field, weighted by meta share, with equal ratings and no first-turn edge. Decks with little evidence shrink toward the ladder mean.

The deck with the best expected win rate leads. Every other deck takes its tier from how many points it sits under the leader:

| Tier | Points under the leader |
|---|---|
| Tier 1 | The leader, plus the next deck within 0.5 |
| Tier 1.5 | Within 0.5, once Tier 1 is full |
| Tier 2 | Up to 3 |
| Tier 3 | Up to 4.5 |
| Tier 4 | More than 4.5 |

Tier 1 holds two decks at most. When the leader's rate moves, the boundaries move with it, so a deck can change tier in a week its own rate held still. A deck needs 0.5% of the meta before it gets a tier. This ladder sets no player minimum, so one specialist can carry a small deck into the tiers.

- **Meta share** is a deck's share of deck-games. Each game counts once per player, mirrors included.
- **Raw win rate** is wins divided by wins, losses and draws. Draws stay in the denominator, games without a result stay out of rates, and the strength fit skips draws.
- **Mirrors** count toward meta share and help estimate the rating and turn-order effects. Raw win rates and matchups leave them out.
- **The 95% interval** shows the uncertainty around expected win rate. We widen it when daily results swing more than sampling noise explains.
- **Decks** take up to 2 archetype names, lead archetype first. A card in at least 10% of decklists counts as a staple, and names no deck, when 50% or more of the lists running it hold no other card of its archetype. We merge equivalent hybrid orders into one key and keep hybrids apart from pure builds.

items.q: What is the best Yu-Gi-Oh! Genesys deck right now?
items.md: Kewl Tune / Synchron, with an expected 60.3% win rate (95% interval 55.5–64.8) at 0.7% of the meta, from ladder games through November 6, 2026.

items.q: What are the Tier 1 decks in Genesys?
What is the most played deck in the Genesys meta?
items.md: Blitzclique, at 6.8% of the meta. It has an expected 57.1% win rate and sits in Tier 3, 3.13 points under the leader.

By distance from the leader in expected win rate. Tier 1 is the leader plus one deck within 0.5 points; further decks within that gap go to Tier 1.5. Tier 2 reaches 3 points under the leader and Tier 3 reaches 4.5; Tier 4 takes the rest. A deck needs 0.5% of the meta to be ranked.

items.q: Why did a deck change tier when its win rate barely moved?
items.md: The tiers count from the leader. When the leader's expected win rate rises or falls, every tier boundary moves with it, and decks near a boundary cross it.

items.q: Is this tier list based on tournament results?
items.md: No. It uses ranked games on YGO Omega. Tournament players can face a different field, so treat the list as a ladder benchmark.

items.q: Does a popular deck get a higher tier?
items.md: No. Blitzclique holds 6.8% of the meta and sits in Tier 3. Angelechy / Dark Time Wizard holds 0.6% and sits in Tier 2.

items.q: How much does going first matter?
items.md: The model estimates a 63.0% win probability going first between equal decks and player ratings on the Genesys ladder. This coefficient uses the games in the fit, including post-side games.

items.q: How often is the tier list updated?
items.md: Every week, on this same page. Each week also gets its own [meta report](/wiki/yu-gi-oh-meta-report-november-6-2026), and the [statistics page](/statistics?ladder=genesys) shows the current numbers between updates.

items.q: Where can I see decklists for these decks?
items.md: The [statistics page](/statistics?ladder=genesys) has sample decklists, card usage and full matchup tables for each deck.
